scenarios.context: A boy tells his sister about his new plan.

speakerA.en: I've decided to learn the guitar this year, Maryam.
I'll take a lesson every Saturday and practise for thirty minutes each day.
My aim is to play a whole song by the summer.
Thanks. Having a plan makes me feel more motivated already.

speakerB.en: That's a great goal. How will you do it?
That's realistic. Small steps are better than big promises.
I'm sure you can do it. I'll listen to you whenever you want.
Write it down and put it on your wall. You'll see it every day.

scenarios.context: Two friends talk about running every morning.

speakerA.en: How's your running plan going, Kian?
Wow, that's impressive. I always give up after the first week.
Don't you ever feel lazy in the morning?
Maybe I could start with you. I need someone to push me.

speakerB.en: Not bad. I've run four days a week for a month now.
I felt the same, but now I keep a record of my progress, and it keeps me going.
Of course, but I remember my goal, and I tell myself that it will get easier.
Sure. We can support each other, and it's more fun together.

scenarios.context: A student failed a test and talks to her father.

speakerA.en: I failed my maths test, Dad. I studied for hours, but I still got a bad mark.
I understood the lesson, but I made many careless mistakes.
What if I fail again? I'm afraid that I'm just not good at maths.
You're right. I'll ask my teacher to explain the parts I didn't understand.

speakerB.en: I'm sorry. Do you know where you went wrong?
Then next time check your answers carefully before you hand in the paper.
Nobody is born good at it. Failure can teach you a lot if you don't give up.
That's the spirit. I'm proud of you for trying again.

scenarios.context: Two students discuss how to get better at English.

speakerA.en: My English hasn't improved much this year. What can I do?
I do that sometimes, but I forget new words very quickly.
Is speaking practice useful too?
That sounds possible. Would you like to be my partner?

speakerB.en: Try to use it every day. Watch films with subtitles and read short stories.
Write them in a notebook and use each one in a sentence. Review them every weekend.
Definitely. Find a partner and talk for ten minutes every day, even if you make mistakes.
With pleasure. If we practise regularly, we'll see the difference in a few months.

scenarios.context: A girl tells her friend about reaching her goal.

speakerA.en: Guess what! I finally finished my first book in English.
Three months. At the beginning I had to use the dictionary on every page.
Proud, and more confident. I'd like to read a longer book next.
Great idea. Hard work should always be celebrated.

speakerB.en: Congratulations, Atefeh! How long did it take you?
That shows how much you've improved. How do you feel now?
Then you should reward yourself first. Let's go and have a pizza.
Yes, and the next goal will feel easier because you know you can do it.
